review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of both equivalences across the TauCeti repo. The one concrete duplication is the pair of group equivalences, `pointsBaseChangeEquiv` and `pointsEquivOfIsPullback`. I did not flag `pointPullback` versus `pointsPullback`: the first is a private helper that the bundled homomorphism uses. I did not flag `left_comp_structureMap`, because I did not find a Mathlib or Batteries counterpart for it. I did not search Mathlib for an existing notion of a section of an Over-object. The duplication is inside this library rather than between this file and Mathlib, so it fits the rubric only through its "same question within Mathlib itself" clause. I have not compiled anything.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def pointsEquivOfIsPullback :
    (𝟙_ (Over S') ⟶ Over.mk E'.structureMap) ≃* (Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk E.structureMap) where
  toFun P := Over.homMk (P.left ≫ g) (by simp [hg.w])
findings.problem: The file defines the same group equivalence twice. `pointsBaseChangeEquiv` (line 154) and `pointsEquivOfIsPullback` (line 391) have the same hypotheses `hg h0` and the same type, `(𝟙_ (Over S') ⟶ Over.mk E'.structureMap) ≃* (Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk E.structureMap)`. Both use `P ↦ homMk (P.left ≫ g)` and the inverse `hg.lift x.left (𝟙 S')`. Their docstrings say the same thing. Each has its own `_left` or `_apply_left` simp lemma, which has the same statement, and a companion lemma for the inverse (`pointsEquivOfIsPullback_symm_apply_left_comp`). The two are not definitionally interchangeable by instance search. Downstream code splits between them: NaiveExactOrder/Basic.lean and YOne.lean use `pointsBaseChangeEquiv`, and ModularCurve/Ell.lean uses `pointsEquivOfIsPullback`. Mixing them requires an unfolding or `rfl` conversion, and the simp lemmas for one do not fire on the other.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one equivalence, e.g. `pointsBaseChangeEquiv`, with its `_left` simp lemma and the `symm` lemma. Delete `pointsEquivOfIsPullback` and its two lemmas. Update the Ell.lean uses (lines ~500–508) to the kept name. If the other name is wanted, make it an `abbrev` or a reducible alias of the kept one rather than a second structure. Update the module docstring, which currently lists both.
findings.benefit: Readers get one canonical equivalence, with one set of simp lemmas, and downstream files no longer choose between two interchangeable names. About 20 lines are removed and the two proofs of `map_mul'` no longer need to be kept in sync.
